title: Graphene-Derived Nanomaterials for Wastewater Treatment: Bridging Laboratory Performance and Practical Feasibility
authors: Sonali Bhatt
abstract: Rapid industrialization and urbanization have increased the discharge of complex pollutants into aquatic systems, posing significant environmental and public health challenges. Conventional wastewater treatment technologies often fail to remove trace contaminants such as pharmaceuticals, heavy metals, and emerging organic compounds. Graphene-based materials, including graphene oxide, reduced graphene oxide, and graphene quantum dots, have emerged as promising candidates due to their high surface area, tunable surface chemistry, mechanical robustness, and unique electronic properties, enabling diverse removal mechanisms such as adsorption, catalysis, and membrane filtration. Laboratory studies have shown that these materials can achieve superior pollutant removal efficiencies; however, their large-scale implementation remains limited, highlighting the gap between laboratory performance and industrial feasibility.This review provides a structured assessment of graphene-based materials for wastewater treatment. Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature review covering 2010–2024 was conducted, with emphasis on the latest 2025 studies addressing techno-economic and industrial feasibility. The review examines the types of graphene materials, their physicochemical properties, and functionalization strategies, followed by critical evaluation of their applications in removing various contaminants. Key research gaps, including aggregation, fouling, regeneration loss, toxicity, and lack of standardized protocols, are discussed. The techno-economic and industrial feasibility section analyzes production costs, scalability, energy requirements, and lifecycle considerations. Finally, future perspectives on AI-guided material design, smart membranes, and regulatory frameworks are outlined to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and practical development.

title: Disciplined Anticipation: The Transdisciplinary Thought Experiments of Stanisław Lem, or How to Use Science Fiction to Responsibly Explore Futures
authors: Julien Bucher
abstract: In the face of technological uncertainty and the inherent pro-innovation bias of contemporary strategy, traditional foresight often lacks the systemic depth required for responsible anticipation. This article proposes a methodological framework for utilizing Science Fiction (SF) not as mere inspiration, but as a disciplined tool for strategic stress-testing. Using a systematic combining approach, the study abductively develops a five-dimensional characterization framework for Thought Experiments (TE), synthesizing classical cognitivist theories with the system-simulation logic of Stanisław Lem. Introducing four units of analysis (Golem XIV, Sexplosion, Weapon Systems, His Master’s Voice), the article illustrates how Lem’s transdisciplinary simulations reveal path dependencies, dynamic system-wide propagation, and breaking points often invisible to linear forecasting. Grounded in Hans Jonas’s Heuristics of Fear, the findings demonstrate that disciplined SF-based TEs provide organizations with a robust epistemic foundation for Responsible Innovation and the identification of long-term systemic risks. title: A Robust RGB Image Encryption Scheme via 3D Henon Map and DNA-Based Techniques
authors: Mahwish Bano, Umair Habib, Hela Elmannai, Mohammed Alkhowaiter, Insaf Ullah
abstract: Chaotic maps are attractive due to their pseudo-randomness, ease of building, and great sensitivity to small changes in the initial value. To provide secure communication during picture scrambling, chaotic maps are typically utilized to generate chaotic keystreams. Recently, several techniques for image encryption were proposed. Some offer a high level of safety, but due to their slow speeds and complex nature, they are rarely used. However, the main motivation behind this research came from a methodology devised by us to encrypt image data through DNA cryptography using the 3D Henon map, considering the issues mentioned above. In the first step of the proposed scheme, the key is generated using a DNA string that serves as a diffusion layer in image encryption. The color channels are then separated from the RGB image. Then, each channel of the image is multiplied by the encryption key generated by DNA cryptography to obtain the partially encrypted image. In the second step, the substitution box is prepared using a simple polynomial that cannot be divided into linear factors. Numerous pairs of points are created by application of the Henon map. One coordinate value is chosen from each point by using the Galois field. If the value is not zero, apply the inverse of the finite field; otherwise, it remains unchanged. At random, select values less than 256. Using these randomly selected values, a substitution box is created. Finally, the Exclusive-OR (XOR) operation is applied between the S-boxes and the partially encrypted image to obtain the final encrypted image. Security tests confirm that the proposed method could be used in real-world image transmission. The 3D Henon map, when combined with DNA cryptography and the S-box-based image encryption technique, provides strong encryption with fast encryption time, as demonstrated by encryption results using digital photographs.

title: A Financial Engineering Framework for Cryptocurrency Portfolio Optimization Based on a Four-Stage Intelligent Decision-Making
authors: B. Adabi Firouzjaee
abstract: This paper presents a four-stage intelligent decision-making framework for cryptocurrency portfolio optimization. In the first stage, statistical anomalies are removed via Isolation Forest algorithm. The second stage establishes the statistical foundations of proposed approach, including exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA), covariance matrix using Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage, and higher-order moments (skewness and kurtosis). The third stage uses a hybrid Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization (GA-PSO) engine with an adaptive multi-moment utility function and institutional constraints to generate three distinct portfolios: conservative, balanced, and aggressive. In the fourth stage, the optimized portfolios are assessed based on out-of-sample data. The proposed framework is evaluated using a dataset of 168 cryptocurrencies and 1,460 daily observations covering the period 2022–2026. The empirical results suggest that the optimized portfolios outperform Bitcoin and the benchmark index during the evaluation period based on four approaches including comparison of the cumulative returns, the risk-adjusted criteria (Sortino and Calmar ratios), maximum drawdown (MDD) of the conservative portfolio and the kernel density estimation (KDE). These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach for cryptocurrency portfolio construction. The main contribution of this study is the integration of anomaly detection, higher-order moment optimization, hybrid metaheuristic search, and institutional portfolio constraints within a unified cryptocurrency portfolio management framework.

title: Comprehensive Review on Pistacia integerrima (Karka-Shringi): A Medicinal Plant with its Phytoconstituents, Ethnomedicinal Uses and Pharmacological Activities
authors: Isha Sharma, Visnu Das, Shruti Thakur, Harsh Kumar Chauhan, Manish Kumar
abstract: Due to their broad range of therapeutic potential, low cost, and comparatively less side effects than manufactured medications, medicinal plants gained significant attention, among medicinal plant Pistacia integerrima has considered more attraction towards because it is rich in phytochemicals. Pistacia integerrima contain many phytochemical and secondary metabolites like flavonoids, alpha-pinene, sterols, terpenoids, kaempferol, catechins, fisetin, m-cymene, fenchyl alcohol, tannins, di-limonene, caprylic acid. The plant is used for many therapeutic activity antibacterial, anti-cancer, anti-asthmatic, anti-fungal, muscle-relaxant activity. Traditionally gall of the plant is used in numerous diseases like in fever, cough, dysentery, snake bite and diarrhoea. The aim of the study is to present medicinal importance, pharmacological activity of Pistacia integerrima.

title: An Efficient Broadcast Encryption Scheme Supporting Decentralized Decryption
authors: Phi Thuong Le, Viet Cuong Trinh
abstract: Broadcast encryption enables the encryption of a plaintext for an arbitrary set of users, each holding a distinct secret key, such that only the designated users can decrypt the ciphertext. Broadcast encryption has numerous practical applications, including pay television, file sharing, and cloud data storage. However, almost all existing broadcast encryption schemes still suffer from an important limitation: they do not support decentralized decryption capability among users. In other words, decryption can be performed using a single secret key alone, which introduces significant security risks in practical deployments. In this paper, we investigate the construction of a broadcast encryption scheme that supports decentralized user decryption capability. Furthermore, our proposed scheme is built upon elliptic-curve cryptographic techniques, rather than relying on the less efficient pairing-based tools adopted by most existing broadcast encryption schemes, and it completely eliminates the key escrow problem inherent in current broadcast encryption systems.

title: Enhancing conceptual understanding and knowledge retention in 11th-grade chemistry classes through inquiry-based pedagogy: a quasi-experimental mixed-methods study
authors: Miguel Ángel Bautista, Xin Chen
abstract: This study examines the impact of inquiry-based pedagogy (IBP) on 11th-grade students’ conceptual understanding and conceptual retention of chemistry concepts in the Dominican Republic. A quasi-experimental, mixed-methods design was employed, involving an experimental group (n = 13) that received inquiry-based instruction through the guided inquiry design (GID) model and a control group (n = 15) that received direct lecture-based instruction over a one-month instructional period. Conceptual understanding and conceptual retention were assessed using adapted versions of the chemistry conceptual reasoning test (CCRT), administered as a pretest, posttest, and delayed test. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), controlling for pretest scores and gender, revealed a statistically significant advantage for the IBP group in overall conceptual understanding (p = 0.006, Cohen's d = 1.20), with stronger effects observed for atomic theory and chemical bonding than for properties of the elements. Results also indicated higher levels of conceptual retention among students exposed to inquiry-based instruction. Qualitative data from semi-structured interviews further elaborated these findings, revealing how inquiry-based pedagogy fostered greater student engagement, deeper reasoning, and more meaningful conceptual understanding through interconnected social, cognitive, and epistemic learning experiences. Overall, the study concludes that inquiry-based pedagogy is a context-sensitive but effective instructional approach for enhancing conceptual learning and retention in secondary-level chemistry, particularly in developing educational contexts, and supports its thoughtful integration into chemistry teaching practices.

title: Indole–hydrazone hybrid derivatives as emerging therapeutics for enhanced skin cancer therapy: molecular design, biological evaluation and nanoliposomal delivery

abstract: To advance skin cancer therapeutics, a series of indole–hydrazone derivatives (5a–5l) was synthesized via the hydrazone condensation reaction and formulation development of 5l -based nanoliposomal gel (GEL4).

title: Empirical study of analogical reasoning in a model experiment on flour-dust explosion
authors: Richard Fisch, Katrin Sommer
abstract: Model experiments are widely used in chemistry education to make inaccessible phenomena tangible, yet the conditions under which learners successfully draw inferences from a model experiment about a real-world phenomenon via analogical reasoning remain unclear. This study examines how young learners use a model experiment on flour-dust explosion to explain an industrial dust explosion incident and identifies prerequisites associated with successful analogical reasoning. We analyzed audio-recorded analogical reasoning processes in 186 parent–child dyads (children's mean age: 9.92 years old) and 114 student–student dyads (mean age: 10.38 years old). Parent–child dyads reached relational mappings for three of the five conditions necessary for a dust explosion to occur, while the more abstract conditions – oxidant as an invisible reactant and confinement as a causal precondition – were frequently left out. Across both dyad types, complementary contributions were observed, with shared analogical reasoning exceeding both partners’ individual contributions in 39.2% of parent–child and 37.7% of student–student dyads. Children's cognitive ability was positively associated with their individual analogical reasoning performance. Parents’ prior knowledge was positively associated with the dyad's shared performance. Compared with student–student dyads, children in parent–child dyads showed higher individual and shared scores. Adjusted analyses indicated an association between dyad type and both outcomes, with the difference being more robust for shared performance. This suggests that young learners may benefit from collaborating with parents when engaging in analogical reasoning. Overall, these findings highlight parents as valuable learning partners for analogical reasoning and motivate instructional implications for the use of model experiments in early chemistry education.

title: Dielectric Pocket and Tri Metal Gate Work Function Tuning for Performance Enhancement of 5 nm Gate All Around Nanowire Field Effect Transistor
authors: B. Shabana, A. Swetha, B. Balaji, Rajyalakshmi Uppada, Sreevardhan Cheerla, D. Sreenivasa Rao, Vipul Agarwal, Y. Gowthami
abstract: This paper presents a simulated study on a 2D Gate-All-Around (GAA) Dielectric Pocket (DP) with a Tri-Metal Nanowire MOSFET, designed to mitigate short-channel effects (SCEs) in 7 nm devices using SOI technology. The proposed architecture incorporates HfO2 dielectric pockets at the source and drain ends, a p-type doped channel, n-type source/drain regions, and a tri-metal gate structure, enclosed by high-k (HfO2) and low-k (SiO2, vacuum) dielectric pairs. Simulations were conducted using Silvaco ATLAS TCAD tool to demonstrate superior electrostatic control, drain currents between 8.4 × 10⁻⁶ A and 1.12 × 10⁻⁵ A, and a subthreshold slope of 63 mV/dec. The device achieves a high transconductance of 1.1 × 10⁻⁵ S, cut off frequencies peaking at 8 × 10⁵ Hz, and FTP of 5 × 10⁵ Hz/V. The Vacuum-Si3N4 produces a maximum gain of 6 dB, highlighting its suitability for high-performance analog and digital applications. Key performance metrics calculated include gate capacitance, gate-source/drain capacitances, drain current, Sqrt (Ids), trans conductance (Gm), subthreshold slope (SS), cut off frequency (fT), FTP, TGF, gain (Av), switching time (τ), Ion, Ioff, Ion / Ioff, band energies, electron mobility, surface potential, electric field, and QFL across various dielectric pairs and gate work functions.

title: Towards direct dynamics simulation of photochemistry without the Born–Oppenheimer approximation
authors: Jong‐Kwon Ha, Edith Leal-Sánchez, Ryan J. MacDonell
abstract: The simulation of photochemical reactions requires a quantum mechanical treatment of electronic and nuclear dynamics. Most simulation approaches use the Born-Oppenheimer (BO) approximation and calculations of nonadiabatic couplings to evolve a wavefunction on a set of BO electronic states. However, the use of BO states presents several challenges, such as discontinuous surfaces, singular terms in the Hamiltonian, and double-valued boundary conditions. We present a direct dynamics approach for molecular vibronic dynamics which does not invoke the BO approximation simply by avoiding diagonalization of the electronic part of the Hamiltonian. By employing a diabatic propagation scheme for the orbitals, we ensure that all electronic terms vary smoothly as a function of nuclear coordinates in a basis of configuration state functions (CSFs). We derive equations of motion for mixed quantum-classical dynamics techniques employing averaged potentials, such that the simulated trajectories evolve on linear combinations of CSF surfaces. We test our approach for lithium hydride and ethylene. In contrast with BO electronic surfaces, we find that all CSF surfaces and couplings are smooth and integrable in the vicinity of conical intersections and weak avoided crossings. Comparisons of the dynamics of photoexcited lithium hydride show that Ehrenfest dynamics reproduce changes in electronic state populations, but lead to over-coherence. Our equations of motion for coupled-trajectory dynamics fail to reduce the over-coherence problem due to the reliance of the derivation on the BO approximation. With further work on the selection of orbitals and the mixed quantum-classical equations of motion, our work shows the potential of a pre-BO wavefunction ansatz for practical nonadiabatic dynamics simulations.

title: The information content of ultrafast observables: spectroscopy and scattering in excited norbornadiene
authors: Joseph C. Cooper, Adam Kirrander
abstract: We assess the sensitivity of time-resolved observables for characterising ultrafast nonadiabatic reaction dynamics. Using the ultrafast (<100 fs) photoisomerisation of norbornadiene as a testbed, we compare the observables for trajectory surface hopping simulations carried out at four different levels of electronic structure theory, SA-CASSCF and XMS-CASPT2 with (2,2) and (4,4) active spaces, resulting in four different sets of dynamics with distinct lifetimes and branching ratios. For each simulation, we calculate time-resolved photoelectron spectra, and electron- and X-ray scattering signals. The observables are critically evaluated and the advantages and disadvantages of each observable for characterising the excited state dynamics are discussed, including the level of theory required to accurately predict the observables and links to recent and future experiments. Broadly, photoelectron spectroscopy tracks electronic character and internal conversion, while X-ray and electron scattering resolve structural dynamics with the potential for additional information relating to electronic structure. We conclude that multimodal detection is required to uniquely constrain the underlying molecular dynamics.

title: Emerging Role of Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical QC and QA and its Applications across the Industry
authors: Nitika Sharma, Sonika Rattan, Atul Sharma, Sharad Sharad S
journal: Journal of Pharmacy Practice and Community Medicine
abstract: Quality Control (QC) and Quality Assurance (QA) are key elements in the pharmaceutical sector. They help to ensure the safety, efficacy and consistency of medicines. This article discusses the purpose of QC and QA for pharmaceutical manufacturing in the modern era and outlines their development, principles and problems relating to the application of technology and universal quality standards. The article reaffirms the need for continuous and seamless improvement in the maintenance of quality system improvements that are responsible for global health standards and that can be applied to licensed drugs in a wide range of settings, ensuring the effectiveness of medicines delivered to patients in a sustainable manner. QC and QA are important components in pharmaceutical production. Their combined function is to ensure that all products are safe, efficient and reliable. As the industry evolves and moves toward digitalization, automation and data-centric systems, QC and QA evolve from reactive functions to predictive and preventive tools. Continuous improvements, regulatory compliance and the adoption of technology will shape the future of pharmaceutical quality. This paper also analyzes the beneficial use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within the pharmaceutical sector throughout all phases, from drug discovery to drug development, as well as in various departments. Besides necessitating less human labor, it also improves the efficacy of clinical research and pharmaceutical output while diminishing the likelihood of mistake. The report examines the existing challenges in the implementation of AI within the pharmaceutical sector. Furthermore, it evaluates existing challenges and proposes remedies.

title: Wind-Aware Multi-UAV Task Allocation for Heterogeneous Offshore Targets: A Hybrid Memetic NSGA-II Approach
authors: Zhaolin Qi, Lun Zhang, Jian Huang
abstract: In offshore marine monitoring, heterogeneous Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) fleets are required to cooperatively perform reconnaissance against three types of targets—point, line, and area—while the spatially non-uniform offshore wind field exerts a first-order influence on the flight time and fuel consumption of fixed-wing UAVs. This paper formulates the corresponding task allocation problem as a bi-objective optimization problem that simultaneously minimizes the fleet makespan and the total fuel consumption. The three types of heterogeneous targets are uniformly abstracted as task nodes characterized by an “entry state—internal monitoring path—exit state” representation; inter-target transfer paths are generated using Dubins curves under the minimum turning radius constraint; and the spatially non-uniform sea-surface wind field, taken directly from the ERA5 100 m wind over the South China Sea (a strong winter NE-monsoon snapshot, 5.9–10.0 m/s across the task area), is incorporated into the computation of flight time and fuel consumption. Building upon the NSGA-II framework, this paper proposes the HM-NSGA-TE algorithm, which adopts a triple-component discrete chromosome encoding to jointly represent the target sequence, UAV assignment, and execution mode, and couples the evolutionary search with exact polynomial-time sub-solvers for the execution-mode assignment (dynamic programming) and the segment-to-UAV assignment (enumeration over the fleet), together with a hybrid heuristic initialization, an adaptive crossover, multi-type mutation operators, and a makespan-bottleneck-oriented Memetic local search. Under a realistic 100 km×100 km offshore scenario, the proposed algorithm is compared with NSGA-II, ACD-NSGA-II, IMOGWO, and two task-specific baselines for heterogeneous-target reconnaissance (OGA-DEMMO and GACO). The results show that HM-NSGA-TE attains the best mean IGD and the best mean Hypervolume of all six methods, with a statistically significant advantage over every competitor—including the strongest task-specific baseline—on both indicators. It therefore yields the best Pareto front approximation in the comparison, at a planning cost of 29.4 s against the 19.6 s of the runner-up and 17.9 s of standard NSGA-II. Scalability experiments across problem instances ranging from 3 to 10 UAVs and 10 to 50 targets show a 100% feasible rate throughout, polynomial growth of both the search and the pre-computation, and a full planning pipeline of under eight minutes even for the largest instance, validating its applicability to practical offshore monitoring missions. This work is scoped as the Stage-1 static pre-allocation stage of a multi-stage planning framework: it produces wind-aware Pareto-optimal task allocations and reference trajectories from reanalysis wind data, and provides the reusable heterogeneous-target and wind-aware cost modelling together with a fast re-solvable solver that the subsequent task-level and resource-level dynamic re-allocation stages build upon. The reported results reflect simulation-level validation rather than real-flight or hardware-in-the-loop deployment. The source code is publicly available at https://atomgit.com/qq_58312832/UWTP.

title: A Secure and Efficient Lattice-Based Conditional Privacy-Preserving Authentication Protocol for VANETs
authors: Xiaopeng Zhou, Yang Xin, Haoyang Dang, Kaiyan Jin, Lei Shi, Minggang Zheng
abstract: Vehicle ad-hoc networks (VANETs) are a research hotspot of intelligent transportation systems (ITS). With the rapid development of connected vehicles, ensuring secure, reliable and efficient information transmission in VANETs has become a critical issue for ITS. To address this problem, this paper proposes an efficient lattice-based conditional privacy-preserving authentication protocol for VANETs. The protocol resists quantum attacks, integrates fog computing to alleviate the authentication burden of trusted authority (TA) and supports batch authentication, which effectively reduces the response delay of VANETs. It is proven to be strongly unforgeable against adaptive chosen-message attacks in the random oracle model. We conducted Java and NS3 simulation experiments on the scheme. Compared with these of some known schemes, the efficiency of a single identity verification operation was improved by 28.89%, and the efficiency of batch verification of 1000 messages was increased by 21.48%. According to the Network Simulator 3 (NS-3) simulation experiments, even in a communication scenario with 400 vehicles and a high driving speed of 25 m/s, the average message loss rate is lower than 3%. The analysis shows that our scheme has obvious advantages in space and computational efficiency.

title: Mutual Information Based Winning Ticket Attention Model for Generic Attack Detection
authors: Brij B. Gupta, Akshat Gaurav, Varsha Arya, Wadee Alhalabi, Ramakrishnan Raman, Kwok Tai Chui
abstract: Modern intrusion detection systems face considerable challenges from generic attacks due to their cryptographic characteristics. In this context, this study proposed a framework for efficient and robust detection of generic attacks. The framework employs Culture Algorithm-based feature selection with mutual information-based sparse attention to select useful feature interactions and suppress interference. The experiment shows that the framework has more than 99% accuracy with an AUC of 0.996. In addition, the framework has a lightweight architecture with just 0.00268M trainable parameters.

title: Next Generation Intelligent Transportation through Disaster Aware Privacy Preserving Federated Learning
authors: T. Srinivasa Rao, D. Venkatarami Reddy, R. Erigela, B. Swetha, B. Balaji
abstract: The growing challenges posed by rapid urbanization and increased vehicle density have highlighted the need for precise and privacy-preserving traffic flow prediction models. Traditional centralized learning methods involve aggregating privacy-sensitive traffic flow data, which poses severe privacy, scalability, and governance issues. To overcome these issues, this paper presents a disaster-aware privacy-preserving federated learning (PP-FL) solution for multi-city traffic flow prediction in heterogeneous and non-IID data settings. Each city separately trains a local deep learning model using local traffic, environmental, and disaster-related data, while only privacy-protected model updates are exchanged with a central aggregator. The proposed solution leverages secure aggregation and differential privacy to ensure data privacy and facilitate efficient cross-city knowledge sharing. Extensive experiments on multi-modal urban traffic datasets, including junction-level surveillance traffic data, highway traffic time-series data, and disaster-influenced traffic data, validate that the proposed solution outperforms state-of-the-art centralized and federated learning baselines by up to 8-12% in RMSE error while substantially mitigating privacy leakage. The results also validate enhanced anomaly detection and disaster-caused traffic disruption prediction performance across cities with limited local traffic data. The obtained results validate the effectiveness of the proposed PP-FL framework as a scalable, secure, and efficient paradigm for next-generation intelligent transportation systems.

title: Detection of Unmarked Non-Metallic Underground Pipelines Using Fine-Grained Strontium Ferrite-Based Powders
authors: I. S. Leonov, Gulnur Zakirova, A. V. Borisov, V. S. Borisova, A. V. Suslova
abstract: An obvious global trend is the spread of plastic pipelines in the construction and repair of underground utilities, including gas distribution pipelines. Despite the advantages of non-metallic pipes, their use is associated with a number of specific problems characteristic of plastic materials. One of such significant problems facing the gas industry is the problem of detecting underground non-metallic utilities and selectively identifying them from adjacent facilities. Pipelines not linked to the global coordinate system in a timely manner can lead to significant economic costs in case of abnormal situations during construction and installation works. The paper investigates an original method of searching for non-metallic utilities associated with the introduction of magnetic powder into the gas flow. It is shown that in the case of the site location in the urban area it is a low-information and ambiguous method. On the contrary, in the open area, in the absence of third-party ferromagnetic interference, this method is not only potentially applicable, but deserves close attention and further research, for which the appropriate design of the test site is proposed. Potential application of the method will increase the informative value of data on the underground location of non-metallic pipelines by 15% for gas distribution pipelines of various diameters, considering the achievement of a magnetic induction level above the pipeline in the range of 60-120 nT.

title: FedMamba-Guard: Federated Mamba State Space Models for Lightweight Anomaly Detection in 6G-Enabled Edge IoT Networks
authors: Mohammed M. Alenazi
abstract: The proliferation of heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) devices at the 6G-enabled network edge introduces critical security vulnerabilities that traditional cloud-centric anomaly detection frameworks are ill-equipped to address. Conventional centralized deep learning approaches impose prohibitive computational overhead on resource-constrained edge nodes, while centralized data aggregation exposes sensitive network telemetry to adversarial exploitation and violates user privacy mandates. To overcome these limitations, we propose FedMamba-Guard, a novel federated learning framework that integrates lightweight Mamba State Space Models (SSMs) for privacy-preserving, real-time intrusion and anomaly detection across distributed edge IoT environments supported by 6G Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) infrastructure. FedMamba-Guard deploys a parameter-efficient Mamba-based local detector at each edge node, exploiting the linear-complexity selective state space mechanism to capture long-range temporal dependencies in network traffic flows without incurring transformer-grade memory costs. A sparse gated aggregation protocol at the 6G MEC server reconciles heterogeneous client updates under non-IID data distributions while preserving differential privacy guarantees through calibrated Gaussian noise injection. To enhance robustness against Byzantine client poisoning attacks, we integrate a Shapley-value-based contribution weighting mechanism that dynamically penalizes malicious participants during global model aggregation. Experiments on the CICIDS-2017, TON-IoT, and UNSW-NB15 benchmarks indicate that FedMamba-Guard achieves a detection accuracy of 98.7%, an F1-score of 98.4%, and a false positive rate of 0.9%, while reducing inference latency by 63% and model parameters by 71% compared to federated transformer baselines under our simulated evaluation setup. Energy consumption per inference cycle is reduced by 58%, suggesting that the framework is well-suited for battery-constrained IoT deployments at the 6G edge; real-world deployment performance may vary with actual 6G hardware and traffic conditions.

title: Key Recovery from Embedded Symmetric-Cipher Key Schedules via Sequential Peeling on Lagrangian Submanifolds
authors: Victoria Mellor, Fahad Ahmad
abstract: We show that a symmetric-cipher key schedule embedded onto a Lagrangian submanifold leaks its key in closed form. In the Lagrangian Balanced Encryption (LBE) construction, each schedule byte sets the kick strength of one iterate of the Chirikov standard map, and the difficulty of identifying a Lagrangian from limited observations is taken to protect the key. Our central result overturns that premise: the tangent-map trace of the embedding is an exact affine function of each key byte once the earlier bytes are fixed. This single algebraic fact turns byte-by-byte recovery from a heuristic into a proof. Identifiability follows in closed form, the recovery estimator is a linear least-squares solve with an analytic error law, and the apparent “multiplicative entanglement” that seems to bind the bytes together is revealed as nothing more than an artefact of observing the system at full depth. Given a depth-stratified tangent-map oracle on an admissible query set, sequential peeling recovers the embedded 120-byte prefix of the Advanced Encryption Standard with a 256-bit key (AES-256) schedule and hence the full 32-byte master key—with zero known key bytes on every trial, and does so identically for Serpent-256, ChaCha20, PRESENT-128, SPECK-128/256 and a SHAKE-driven control: recovery is a property of the embedding, and any cipher embedded this way inherits it. The method is fast (one linear solve per byte), robust (100% up to 10−4 relative observation noise, matching the analytic law), independently validated against an extended-precision oracle, and reproduced by a chosen-plaintext variant that uses only momentum observations, while every full-depth zero-knowledge optimiser we tried fails below 5%. The one prerequisite is that the embedding expose its depth-stratified geometry—a conventionally deployed cipher does not, and is unaffected.

title: Intelligent Large-Scale IoT: A Survey on Architectures, Learning, and Autonomous Decision-Making
authors: Ateeq Ur Rehman, Gayathre Vaidyanathan, Kirubavathi Ganapathiyappan
abstract: The rapid emergence of large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) systems leads to massive heterogeneous data generation, which raises significant challenges in scalability, semantic interoperability, security, and autonomous decision-making. Existing state-of-the-art surveys primarily focus on individual technologies such as Deep Learning (DL), Federated Learning (FL), or IoT security, in isolation, providing limited insight into their integration for realizing intelligent IoT ecosystems. To address this gap, this survey presents a comprehensive data-to-decision framework that encompasses the entire intelligent IoT pipeline, including data acquisition, communication architectures, distributed intelligence, semantic interoperability, security, and autonomous decision-making. Specifically, this survey includes both centralized and distributed intelligence paradigms, including DL, FL, and Automated Machine Learning (AutoML), together with semantic interoperability methods based on knowledge graphs and learning-based security mechanisms. Additionally, we investigate intelligent decision-making approaches, with particular emphasis on Reinforcement Learning (RL) and multi-agent systems for enabling autonomous IoT operations. A systematic analysis of existing approaches is provided, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and integration challenges. Finally, we identify key research gaps and outline promising future directions, including foundation models, edge-native generative artificial intelligence, digital twins, continual learning, and trustworthy autonomous IoT systems.

title: HT-FairGNN: High-Threshold Fairness for Graph Neural Networks via Soft Survival-Function Alignment
authors: Hua Tan, Zhongyi Zhai, Lingzhong Zhao, Shike Long
abstract: Fairness observed for graph neural networks (GNNs) at a conventional decision threshold need not remain stable under stricter high-threshold decision rules, a deployment issue that we term fixed-threshold fairness fragility. To address this problem, we propose HT-FairGNN, a model-agnostic in-processing framework based on high-threshold soft survival-function alignment (HTSFA), which aligns group-wise soft survival functions over an application-relevant high-threshold region using differentiable soft-threshold estimators; we further establish soft-to-hard bounds showing that the HTSFA objective controls empirical hard-threshold Statistical Parity (SP) and Equal Opportunity (EO) disparities up to terms determined by near-threshold score mass and sigmoid approximation error. Across five benchmark datasets, HT-FairGNN reduces average high-threshold SP and EO disparities by roughly two-thirds relative to FairGNN, while predictive-utility outcomes vary across datasets and evaluation metrics. Overall, the results support the effectiveness of HT-FairGNN in improving high-threshold fairness under the evaluated settings, subject to dataset- and metric-dependent utility trade-offs.

title: A Comprehensive Methodology for the Integrated Assessment of Road Safety of Transport and Technological Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic
authors: Ravil Safiullin, A. V. Sorvanov, Присяжнюк Михаил Сергеевич, Ravil Safiullin, Andrey Fadeevich Zalyubovskiy
abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. To implement a comprehensive assessment, an algorithm has been proposed that performs automated multi-criteria analysis by merging key safety indicators related to technical condition, driver behavior, and operational factors. This algorithm calculates an integrated safety assessment, ranks carriers by risk level, and identifies potential violations. A method of adaptive membership functions has been applied to handle uncertainty and qualitative parameters. A verification study was conducted on theoretical cases covering a range of operational scenarios. A software solution — a Python module for fuzzy inference and visualization has also been implemented, expanding the capabilities of intelligent transportation systems. The results demonstrate that the developed system correctly ranks transport enterprises by risk level. Verification on five theoretical cases (TK1-TK5) confirmed the model's ability to generate an Integrated Safety Assessment (ISA) from 0 to 1, effectively distinguishing between exemplary compliance and systematic critical violations. For instance, a critically problematic scenario (TK4) received a low ISA of 0.34, signaling the need for immediate intervention, while a case with systematic violations (TK5) scored 0.55, near the predefined acceptability threshold of 0.5.

title: Modular integration of MRSF-TDDFT, NAMD, and QM/MM for excited-state dynamics on the OpenQP platform
authors: Mohsen Mazaherifar, Woojin Park, Simone Bonfrate, Jingbai Li, Miquel Huix‐Rotllant, Cheol Ho Choi
abstract: A balanced and efficient description of excited states is essential for accurately capturing ultrafast relaxation processes. In this context, the recently developed mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT) has demonstrated strong performance. However, its broader applicability to realistic systems requires seamless integration with multiscale simulation frameworks. In this work, we present a modular strategy that integrates MRSF-TDDFT with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics (NAMD) and electrostatic potential fitting (ESPF)-based QM/MM embedding methodologies, in which OpenQP (Open Quantum Platform) serves as a modular electronic-structure backend. To further enhance usability and interoperability, we introduce the Open Simulation Manager (OpenSM), a high-level orchestration framework that unifies QM, QM/MM, and NAMD workflows through a consistent and minimal input interface. The resulting OpenQP-OpenSM provides a flexible and extensible platform for multiscale excited-state simulations, enabling rapid integration of advanced electronic-structure methods and fostering collaborative development.

title: Active delta-learning for surface hopping: efficient fitting of potential energy surfaces
authors: Mikołaj Martyka, Joanna Jankowska, Pavlo O. Dral
abstract: Active learning has become central to modern machine-learning workflows for trajectory surface hopping, enabling automatic construction of training sets for excited-state potentials. However, currently used protocols can struggle with convergence, requiring large datasets and extensive human intervention. Here, we combine active learning with Δ-learning - where the ML model predicts the difference between a target quantum chemical method and a computationally efficient baseline - into an end-to-end protocol for active delta-learning (ADL) of potential energy surfaces for trajectory surface hopping dynamics. The protocol is tested on a benchmark system, fulvene, where a twofold data efficiency is achieved with respect to fine-tuning from a pre-trained foundational model, OMNI-P2x. Next, we analyze the case of PSB4, a protonated Schiff base with multiple competing torsional deactivation channels. Here, pure ML active learning fails to converge despite extensive sampling of over 14 000 points, while ADL converges within just two iterations and 900 sampled points, yielding good agreement with the reference.

title: Developing a Strategic Model for the Use of Blockchain Technology: A Qualitative Study
authors: Kaveh  Mangoli Kahtuee, Hamid Esmaeeli, Narges Norouzi, Razieh Keshavarzfard
journal: Tiknuluzhī dar kār/āfarīnī va mudīriyyat-i istrātizhīk.
abstract: This study aimed to develop a strategic model for the use of blockchain technology by identifying and explaining the causal, contextual, and intervening conditions, strategies, and consequences associated with its strategic organizational adoption. This applied, exploratory qualitative study was conducted using the grounded theory approach. Participants comprised experts, managers, specialists, and professionals with knowledge and practical experience in blockchain technology, digital banking, information technology, and strategic management. Participants were recruited through purposive sampling, and data collection continued until theoretical saturation was achieved. Data were primarily collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews. Analysis was conducted through open, axial, and selective coding. During axial coding, concepts and categories were systematically organized according to causal conditions, contextual conditions, intervening conditions, strategies, and consequences. Selective coding was subsequently employed to integrate the categories around the core phenomenon and construct the final strategic model. Constant comparison, data review, and expert confirmation of selected findings were used to enhance the credibility of the analysis. The analysis indicated that strategic blockchain adoption is a multidimensional phenomenon shaped by interdependent technological, organizational, economic, regulatory, and sociocultural factors. Inadequate technological and data-security infrastructure, poor data integration and intelligent analytics, operational inefficiencies, resource constraints, weak data-driven culture, insufficient digital transformation leadership, and governance deficiencies emerged as major causal conditions. Digital-market dynamics, data-driven policymaking, organizational capacity, and social trust constituted important contextual conditions, whereas technological maturity, development and cybersecurity costs, regulatory frameworks, and public trust functioned as intervening conditions. The principal strategies included developing secure and integrated blockchain and data infrastructures, establishing blockchain-oriented digital transformation roadmaps, redesigning organizational processes, creating data-driven revenue models, strengthening regulatory frameworks, enhancing digital literacy and technology acceptance, supporting blockchain startups, and implementing pilot projects. Successful blockchain implementation extends beyond technological deployment and requires an integrated strategic framework aligning technology with organizational structure, business processes, human resources, regulatory requirements, digital leadership, organizational culture, and public trust. A gradual progression from awareness and capacity building to pilot implementation, infrastructure development, and institutionalization may therefore facilitate sustainable and strategically aligned blockchain adoption.

title: Hybrid Metaheuristic Optimization for Time Series Forecasting: Integrating Grey Wolf and Greylag Goose Strategies
authors: Ghassan AL-Thabhawee, Hussein Alkattan
journal: Journal of artificial intelligence and metaheuristics.
abstract: Time series forecasting is crucial in agricultural markets, where accurate predictions can enhance stakeholder decision-making. Traditional statistical models such as ARIMA often struggle with capturing complex patterns, necessitating the integration of metaheuristic optimization techniques to improve predictive performance. This study introduces a novel hybrid optimizer, the Grey Wolf-Greylag Goose Optimizer (GGGWO), which combines the strengths of the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and the Greylag Goose Optimizer (GGO) to enhance the forecasting accuracy of ARIMA models. The proposed GGGWO-ARIMA model is evaluated on a dataset of daily potato prices across multiple Indian cities and is compared against ARIMA, WOA-ARIMA, PSO-ARIMA, GWO-ARIMA, and GGO-ARIMA. Experimental results demonstrate that GGGWO achieves the lowest MSE (0.0027), RMSE (0.0184), and MAE (0.0116) while attaining the highest R-squared (0.9648) and Willmott Index (0.9565), outperforming all baseline models. These findings highlight the efficacy of hybridizing GWO and GGO, offering a robust optimization framework for improving time series forecasting in agricultural price prediction. This can aid policymakers, farmers, and market analysts make data-driven decisions.

title: Learning lattice parameters from powder X-ray diffraction data using invariants
authors: E. Hofgard, Kyucheol Min, Nofit Segal, David Moreau, Aria Mansouri Tehrani, Vanessa Oklejas, Rafael Gómez‐Bombarelli, Jigyasa Nigam
journal: Acta Crystallographica Section A Foundations and Advances
abstract: We present a machine learning (ML) method to determine unit-cell parameters from powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) data using a novel invariant lattice representation. In ML, the data representation used can have a substantial impact on the prediction quality. Previous approaches have directly predicted lattice parameters (a, b, c, α, β, γ) from XRD inputs. However, these parameters depend strongly on the unit-cell reduction or convention used. In this work, we construct an invariant representation of the reciprocal lattice that is independent of primitive-cell convention, based on the bispectrum - a descriptor built from spherical harmonic projections of lattice points. The calculation of the lattice bispectrum is differentiable, and we demonstrate how to invert it using gradient-based optimization initialized from a nearest-neighbor lookup. We show that, with a fixed ML model architecture, using the lattice bispectrum as the ML target rather than the unit-cell parameters leads to more accurate lattice parameter predictions. For example, using the MP-20 dataset, a subset of the Materials Project database, the bispectrum reduces length mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) from 11.08% to 2.43% and angle MAPE from 12.15% to 2.45% compared with direct prediction with the same model architecture. We additionally benchmark our approach against pre-existing XRD data to crystal structure models such as Crystalyze and assess its performance on experimental data. Beyond unit-cell representation, we anticipate this invariant lattice representation could serve more broadly as a geometry-aware target for other crystallographic ML tasks such as structure generation.

title: From reproducibility to comparability in computational photochemistry: lessons from the PhotoChem explorer prototype
authors: Nanna Holmgaard List, Sandra Gómez, Lea M. Ibele, Basile F. E. Curchod, Davide Avagliano
abstract: We present the PhotoChem Explorer (PCE) prototype, a proof-of-concept web-based platform that represents computational photochemistry studies of gas-phase molecules in a structured and queryable form. Rather than treating excited-state dynamics simulations as isolated results reported in heterogeneous formats and across different sources, PCE organizes studies according to their molecular systems, computational workflows, methodological choices, and associated observables, facilitating that relationships and trends can be explored systematically across studies. In this way, the prototype illustrates how structured data representations could support improved findability, comparison, reproducibility, and reuse in computational photochemistry. At a fundamental level, it demonstrates how excited-state dynamics studies could become part of a more connected and cumulative body of knowledge, potentially enabling new modes of investigation. The prototype exposes practical challenges that must be addressed to realize this vision, including the development of shared representations, workflow descriptions, and their integration into scientific practice. More broadly, PCE is intended as a practice-driven experimentation platform to stimulate discussion and iterative community development of standards and representations for excited-state dynamics studies.

title: Bridging the intention–behavior gap in psychologically informed musculoskeletal rehabilitation: A con-vergent mixed-methods investigation and the triadic care model
authors: Atena Mahmoudi
abstract: While clinical guidelines strongly endorse psychologically informed physiotherapy (PIP) and cognitive-behavioral techniques (CBT) for musculoskeletal pain, routine clinical uptake remains inconsistent.Most implementation research describes clinician attitudes without modeling the cognitive and systemic mechanisms that impede translation into daily practice.This study investigates the "intention-behavior gap" in psychologically informed musculoskeletal rehabilitation among Iranian physiotherapists using the COM-B (Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation -Behavior) framework and introduces the Triadic Care Model as an operational solution.A convergent mixed-methods design (QUAN + QUAL) compliant with the Good Reporting of A Mixed Methods Study (GRAMMS) guidelines was conducted between 2023 and 2024.The quantitative phase surveyed 450 licensed physiotherapists using the validated Psychological Practice and Skills Tool (PPST).Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) tested hypothesized paths linking psychological self-efficacy, systemic barriers, postgraduate education, and clinical utilization.The qualitative phase comprised semi-structured, in-depth interviews with 20 practicing physiotherapists analyzed via reflexive thematic analysis.Quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated via a joint display matrix.A pronounced intention-behavior gap was identified: 78.2% (n=352) of clinicians strongly endorsed the bio psychosocial model, yet only 24.4% (n=110) routinely implemented psychological techniques.SEM demonstrated excellent fit (χ2/df=2.15,CFI=.96,TLI=.95,RMSEA=.048[90% CI: .041-.055],SRMR=.042).Psychological self-efficacy directly predicted technique utilization (β=.41, p<.001), while postgraduate training indirectly enhanced utilization via self-efficacy (β=.34, p<.001).Systemic barriers exerted a potent negative direct effect on implementation (β=-.46,p<.001).Qualitative synthesis revealed four systemic-cognitive impediments: (1) The Reimbursement Trap and Tariff Disincentives, (2) Sociocultural Stigmatization and Somatic Fixation, (3) Referral Anxiety and Boundary Ambiguity, and (4) Didactic versus Experiential Pedagogical Deficits.Physiotherapists experience high motivational readiness but severe capability and opportunity deficits.Bridging this gap requires moving beyond generic bio psychosocial advocacy toward structural reimbursement reform, experiential micro-skills training, and the adoption of the Triadic Care Model, a structured interprofessional framework linking the physiotherapist, clinical psychologist, and patient through a warm-referral pathway.

title: Blood Pressure Estimation Based on the Fusion of Features Extracted from Photoplethysmography and Electrocardiography Signals
authors: N. Ghanbari, M. R. Pourmir
abstract: In this paper a novel noninvasive procedure for blood pressure estimation according to the fusion of features extracted from photoplethysmography (PPG) and electrocardiography (ECG) signals is presented. The main goal of the suggested approach is to improve cardiovascular monitoring accuracy by exploiting the complementary information provided by these two physiological signals. In the proposed method PPG and ECG signals are first preprocessed, and a set of 21 blood pressure related physiological features is extracted. These features are then used as predictor variables (inputs) for a set of multivariate linear regression models to estimate blood pressure values. To assess the performance of the presented method, a dataset consisting of multiple signal recordings collected from different patients is utilized. Data preprocessing is carried out through principal component analysis (PCA) while feature dimensionality reduction and selection of the most informative features are achieved through stepwise linear regression. Finally three features exhibiting the highest correlation with blood pressure are identified and selected as the core features of the suggested approach. The effectiveness of the suggested approach is compared with existing methods, and the obtained results demonstrate that the suggested model achieves acceptable accuracy and satisfactory efficiency in blood pressure estimation.

title: A data-efficient machine-learning approach for modeling the photodynamics of all- trans hexatriene based on multireference configuration interaction calculations
authors: Luan G. F. dos Santos, Julio C. V. Chagas, Mikołaj Martyka, Pavlo O. Dral, Mario Barbatti, Francisco B. C. Machado, Richard A. Messerly, Hans Lischka
abstract: Accurate simulations of excited-state photodynamics of polyenes remain challenging due to the high computational cost of multireference electronic-structure methods required to describe the coexistence of ionic and covalent states. In this work, active learning together with machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIP) trained on multireference configuration interaction with single and double excitations (MR-CISD) level energies and gradients, is used to enable efficient and accurate nonadiabatic molecular dynamics for all-trans-hexatriene. A compact yet representative training set is constructed by reducing an initial pool of ∼850 k configurations to ∼3 k geometries while preserving the regions of configurational space relevant for the dynamics. The resulting model reproduces the topology of the excited-state potential energy surfaces and yields a physically consistent relaxation mechanism, characterized by a sequential S2 → S1 → S0 pathway and time constants in good agreement with experimental data. Analysis of representative trajectories provides mechanistic insight into the structural factors governing nonadiabatic transitions, and identifies a notably broader and more diffuse structural distribution associated with the S1 → S0 transition in comparison to the more localized S2 → S1 decay pathway. Analysis of the torsional angles around the CC double bonds reveals preferential isomerization at the central C3C4 bond, providing semi-quantitative evidence for the initiation of cis-trans photoisomerization in the hot ground state. The MLIP simulations trained at high-level MR-CISD are extremely efficient, enabling 200 trajectories running up to 800 fs in short time, whereas direct on-the-fly multireference dynamics simulations would be practically impossible at this MR level.

title: Data-Driven Voltage Control for Distribution Networks with High Penetration of PVs via Improved DDPG
authors: Xiaolong Xiao, Linghao Zhang, Ziran Guo, Xiaoxing Lu, Wenqiang Xie, Shukang Lv, Peishuai Li
abstract: The highly increasing integration of distributed photovoltaics (PVs) has brought significant challenges for distribution network voltage control, which struggles with fast and stochastic fluctuations. This paper proposes a data-driven voltage control method utilizing an improved deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) to minimize power losses while maintaining voltage within a safe operating range. The data-driven voltage control framework is established first, with the controlling center formulated as the agent. Based on the distribution network system and the voltage control original model, the data-driven voltage control model is formulated via the Markov decision process (MDP). A voltage sensitivity-guided DDPG algorithm, which incorporates the voltage-reactive power injection sensitivity matrix into the actor policy gradient, is developed to embed physical grid knowledge and reduce the actor’s reliance on critic action-gradient estimates, thus the practicality and generalization of data-driven voltage control is improved. Numerical simulations on the modified IEEE 33-node test system show the method maintains all nodal voltages within limits and reduces total system losses under varying PV generation, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for future sustainable power systems.

title: Closed-Loop QUBO-Guided Formulation Optimization for Enzyme Fermentation: An Industrial Case Study
authors: Chia-Ho Ou, Wen-Chih Chang, Ying-Wei Tseng, Yu-Ting Kao, Yeong-Jar Chang, Jin-Jia Wang
abstract: Enzyme formulation discovery requires repeated evaluation of combinations of process and ingredient settings, making unguided experimentation costly. This study presents a QUBO-based closed-loop optimization framework for an industrial enzyme-fermentation case study. The physical optimization loop uses a 22-bit one-hot encoding, whereas a separate 625-bit instance is used only for solver benchmarking. Three implementation components address different bottlenecks: the Walking-in-the-Snow procedure augments sparse early-stage data and removes synthetic samples near newly observed formulations; the coarse-to-fine strategy first calibrates linear and constant terms before refining the full stored coefficient set; and a contour-aware weighted loss emphasizes formulations near the best active-ingredient (AIN) values observed to date. The guided program reached an AIN value of 10,068 at cumulative experiment index 405, compared with a prior unguided best of 8481, an 18.7% increase in the best observed value. Independent evidence is provided by 17 prospective sequential prediction–experiment pairs generated after the 18-sample initialization set; these yielded an MAE of 239.29 AIN units, an RMSE of 264.55, a MAPE of 2.54%, and R2 = 0.473. A descriptive benchmark on the common 625-bit QUBO compared D-Wave Hybrid, Fujitsu DA3, the Compal GPU Annealer (CGA), and classical simulated annealing (SA) under the recorded time budgets. The study does not claim quantum advantage, a universal SA complexity result, a controlled trial-reduction percentage, or component-wise ablation. Instead, it provides a transparent industrial case study of QUBO-guided sequential experimentation and states the limits of the available evidence.

title: Unified adiabatic and diabatic excited-state description via the ensemble-variational quantum eigensolver
authors: Christophe Soule, Bruno Senjean, Benjamin Lasorne
abstract: Within the present noisy intermediate-scale quantum-computing era, hybrid quantum-classical-processor algorithms have emerged as promising avenues for tackling electronic-structure eigenproblems. Among them, the so-called ensemble-variational quantum eigensolver has been designed to treat ground and excited states on an equal footing and proven effective in capturing features such as conical intersections and avoided crossings between two electronic states, as we recently demonstrated for formaldimine. We also showed in that example how the underlying ensemble-variational principle was prone to providing a quasi-diabatic representation "for free". To date, this method has been limited to computing only two eigenstates of a Hamiltonian. The aim of the present paper is to show how and under what conditions this can be generalized to models that involve three or more coupled electronic states. Our approach relies on designing a parameterized basis transformation that can directly be implemented on a quantum computer for further post-treatment. This nontrivial step is accompanied by the development of quantum circuits specifically adapted to the several states of interest. An algebraic optimization strategy for the parameters of the basis transformation is formulated to obtain the target eigenstates as well as the optimally diabatic states under various objective flavors of the ensemble-variational principle. Our approach was tested for addressing the first three coupled electronic states of the H+4 molecular ion as a proof of principle, with three electrons in four spatial orbitals, along various geometries.

title: Where Does the Agreement Come from? An Agreement-source Test for Rank-order Key Transport on Commodity Wi-Fi RSSI
authors: Riyadh Hadinah Ahtar Lakadimu, Mike Yuliana, Tita Karlita, Nailul Muna, Hendri Darmawan, Moch. Zen Samsono Hadi, Gallyndra Fatkhu Dinata, Refa Firgiyanto
journal: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
abstract: Physical-layer key generation is commonly evaluated by how often two nodes disagree before correction, assuming agreement originates from the wireless channel.Inputs shared by construction can carry rank-order information, so disagreement rate alone cannot identify the source of agreement.We investigate this using ETRCP-LE, a rank-order key-transport construction for commodity Wi-Fi RSSI, combining shared-step ablation, a no-channel adversary holding public parameters, and an identity control.Over eleven sessions that adversary reproduces 221 of 420 indoor rounds against the receiver's 112; on ten preregistered hold-out sessions, 136 of 529 outdoor rounds against 43 and 105 of 291 indoor against 44.Agreement is driven predominantly by a public multiplier.A counterconfiguration without it, recovering 7 of 14 outdoor rounds in the main campaigns, does not replicate: on the hold-out the receiver recovers 9 of 81 and channel-free parties 4 of 86.Low disagreement alone does not establish channel-derived agreement.

title: PoCA-Mithril: A Blockchain-enabled Framework for Identity- and Context-verifiable Communication among Distributed AI Agents
authors: Kranthi Kumar Gunda, Geetha Arjunan
journal: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
abstract: Distributed Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems face challenges in agent identity verification, context integrity, traceability, and scalable blockchain anchoring without a continuously trusted central authority.This paper proposes PoCA-Mithril, a blockchain framework for verifiable agent communication.Proof-of-Context Attestation (PoCA) signs agent identity, context, timestamp, and safety metadata.A Mithril-Inspired Relay (MR) batches proofs via Merkle trees and a SHA-256 signature digest before Solidity smart-contract anchoring.Prototype (Python, Web3.py, decentralized identifiers, Ganache, web interface) averaged 1.2555, 1.9402, and 3.5815 ms for Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) keypair generation, PoCA generation, and verification.Relay aggregation stays below 0.04 ms; five-proof batching cuts transactions 80%.It authenticates identity and context metadata, not complete response-content integrity.Persistent request-ID storage with database-enforced uniqueness rejects duplicates; restart and shared-database tests confirmed persistence.Five-process concurrency yielded one accepted claim, four duplicate rejections; multi-server verification remains unevaluated.An AgentDID-inspired baseline and 10,000-operation workloads characterize the local prototype, not distributed-blockchain performance.Response-content binding, model artifact, and runtime-execution verification remain future work.

title: Offset-normalised Savitzky–Golay Channel Smoothing for Key Agreement in Heterogeneous LoRa V2X: Unified Benchmarking and Ablation Study
authors: Rini Puji Astutik, Mike Yuliana, Wenny Mistarika Rahmawati, Nailul Muna, Reni Soelistijorini, Tri Budi Santoso
journal: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
abstract: Physical-Layer key agreement using RSSI from heterogeneous LoRa transceivers is impaired by a persistent node-dependent RSSI reporting difference of 9.5-12.7 dB between the RFM95 and SX1262 modules, elevating prereconciliation key disagreement rate (KDR).This study proposes an offset-normalised Savitzky-Golay pipeline that corrects the node-dependent bias through median offset calibration followed by polynomial smoothing.The pipeline is evaluated on field measurements from eight LoRa V2V and V2I mobility conditions at 20-30 km/h and benchmarked against four baselines under a common evaluation protocol.An eight-configuration ablation study confirms offset normalisation as an effective first-stage correction (7.5% KDR reduction [50/25/25 split]) with Savitzky-Golay providing a further 22.4% reduction; BiLSTM prediction increases KDR to 0.4150 under the available dataset (50 or fewer training samples in seven of eight conditions).The Offset-SavGol configuration achieves KDR 0.1375 (V2I Straight, [60/20/20 split]) and median KDR 0.2417 (IQR 0.1222, [50/25/25 ablation split]); under a multi-objective criterion (median KDR, inter-condition IQR, degenerate output), Savitzky-Golay and Moving Average (median KDR 0.1302) are both non-dominated smoothing candidates.In the unified benchmark, the Offset-SavGol configuration attains agreed KGR of 0.8734 bps (highest among all seven evaluated pipelines) and total pure processing time of 3.67 ms on Raspberry Pi 5 (excluding acquisition interval) without model training.Security against eavesdropping remains subject to future investigation.

title: NeevAs An AEAD Design for Lightweight Cryptography
authors: Varsha Jarali, Hari Preeth S, Khushboo Bussi, Shashi Kant Pandey
abstract: Authenticity and confidentiality are crucial for maintaining a secure information infrastructure. Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure, while authenticity ensures origin of the data. Authenticated encryption ensures both simultaneously by protecting data from access and verifying integrity. This paper presents a NeevAs cipher suite offering authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD) and hashing, based on a sponge-based duplex construction. The scheme included concurrent absorption, a novel sponge method, where associated data is absorbed into the capacity part and plaintext into the rate part simultaneously. This reduces permutation calls typically required for associated data processing compared to existing sponge based designs. In the NeevAs cipher suite, the modified Neeva hash function generates the security tag, and the Ascon S-box provides efficiency and resistance against differential and boomerang attacks. The design targets lightweight cryptography, minimizing permutation calls to enhance efficiency and reduce resource consumption, making it well-suited for resource-constrained devices.

title: SECURING BIG DATA IN THE INTERNET OF THINGS (IOT): PRIVACY AND SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS
authors: Naveed Hussain
journal: Journal of Big Data Privacy Management
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming industries by connecting billions of devices and enabling the generation and collection of vast amounts of data, commonly referred to as Big Data. While this data presents numerous opportunities for innovation, it also raises significant privacy and security concerns. This paper explores the security and privacy challenges in securing Big Data within the IoT ecosystem, and proposes frameworks and techniques for addressing these issues. By examining existing vulnerabilities, security protocols, and emerging technologies, the study provides recommendations for ensuring data protection in the IoT environment. Key challenges such as data encryption, access control, and secure data transmission are discussed, alongside solutions like blockchain and federated learning for enhancing privacy in IoT systems.

title: Kissing Number of Codes: A Survey
authors: Yi Liu, Wei Kuang Cheng, Olivier Rioul, Sylvain Guilley, Patrick Solé
abstract: The kissing number of a code is the average number of pairs of codewords at minimum distance from each other. It has fundamental applications in determining code performance. Besides, a recent interest has arisen from the field of side-channel analysis of algorithms handling sensitive information (e.g., cryptographic keys). Namely, when code-based masking protections are applied, their performance in terms of the attacker's signal-to-noise ratio or mutual information is proportional to the kissing number of the masking code. Therefore, the kissing number is also a security metric for a given minimum distance in side-channel-protected implementation, as it is in code performance evaluation. It is known exactly for some classical families of codes. To estimate it in general, two types of bounds are given. Linear programming, either numerically or by the polynomial method, is the most versatile and the more precise. Spectral graph theory provides bounds on the multiplicity of the subdominant eigenvalue that are easier to state.

title: Computational investigation on binding interactions of the small Ag6 nanoparticle cluster with histamine neurotransmitter
authors: Anoop Kumar Pandey, Ehsan Shakerzadeh, Radha Singh, Devdutt Chaturvedi
abstract: In this communication, the interaction between the silver nanoparticle cluster (Ag6) with neurotransmitter histamine (C5H9N3) is investigated. The molecular structure, electronic properties and thermo-chemical parameters of the Ag6 complexes with histamine are analyzed. The different configurations of the complexes are explored, with the best adsorption energy occurring in configuration-A where the amino group of the histamine is found to interact well with the Ag6 cluster. According to the electronic analysis, energy gap of histamine becomes significantly decreased after adsorption, so electrical conductivity is increased. The Fermi level and work function of the Ag6 cluster are changed and can affect the emission properties. The complex undergoes thermo-chemical analysis to derive information about its overall thermal energy, specific heat, entropy and Gibbs free energy change. The results provide insight into the thermodynamics and stability of the Ag6@histamine complex that could be exploited for bio-sensing and drug design applications.

title: Bushbaby Optimization Algorithm: A Nature-inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Approach for Engineering Applications
authors: Zeinab Montazeri, Mohammad Dehghani, Raed Abu Zitar, Omar Almomani, Widi Aribowo, Om Parkash Malik, Kei Eguchi
journal: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
abstract: Metaheuristic optimization algorithms are widely used to solve optimization problems; however, designing distinct search mechanisms for exploration and exploitation remains an important research challenge.A new algorithm, Bushbaby Optimization Algorithm (BOA), inspired by the behaviour of the bushbaby, is introduced in this paper.The animal's natural behaviour regarding movement, foraging, and hunting is examined, and two specific behaviours are selected to design the search mechanisms."Nocturnal spatial movement and foraging activity", modeled to facilitate global search, expand search space coverage, and mitigate the risk of premature convergence, forms the basis of the exploration phase.Conversely, the "prey attack and return movement" behaviour is utilized to design the exploitation phase, serving as a mechanism for local search and refinement within promising regions.These behaviours are modeled as algorithmic abstractions within BOA and function as complementary mechanisms to manage the optimization process.The performance of BOA is evaluated using the CEC 2011 test suite, and the results are compared with existing metaheuristic optimization algorithms.The results demonstrate that BOA achieves the top rank in 19 out of 22 problems, representing a success rate of 86.36%.These findings indicate that BOA effectively balances exploration and exploitation and is suitable for a wide range of metaheuristic optimization problems.

title: A LITERATURE REVIEW OF RADIAL BASIS FUNCTION NEURAL NETWORKS FOR BLAST EXPLOSIVE PREDICTION
authors: Fakroul Ridzuan Hashim, Muhamad Izzuddin Abd Rahman, Kamsani Kamal, Mohd Fauzy Mohd  Nor, Mohammed Alias Yusof, Suwimol Jungjit
journal: Journal of Defence Science Engineering & Technology
abstract: This review paper examines the development and application of Radial Basis Function Neural Networks (RBFNN) for predicting blast explosive effects. Addressing the complexities of nonlinear and multi-physics blast phenomena, it highlights the advantages of data-driven approaches over traditional analytical methods. The paper presents the fundamentals of RBF networks, including their architecture, training techniques, and optimization strategies, emphasizing their capacity for universal function approximation and adaptability. A broad range of application domains such as mechanical control systems, energy and environmental modelling, medical diagnostics, and materials science underscore the versatility of RBF models. Performance evaluations demonstrate their robustness and accuracy in handling nonlinearities and uncertainties, although challenges related to computational complexity and data limitations persist. The review discusses hybrid modelling approaches and emerging methodologies like quantum kernels and interpretable artificial intelligence to address existing gaps. Ultimately, this synthesis underscores the significant potential of RBF neural networks in advancing blast effect prediction and suggests pathways for future research integrating novel computational techniques to further enhance prediction accuracy and reliability.

title: LLMs, Neurosymbolics, Semantic AI. and Reality
authors: Jim Brander
journal: Journal of Advances in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
abstract: A comparison of how LLMs, Neurosymbolics and Semantic AI handle a piece of legislation running to 400 pages. Its structure is typical of legislation, specifications, legal agreements, contracts, where a misunderstood word may cost millions to billions, or someone’s life.

title: Perspectives on Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computing: Integer Factoring, Discrete Logarithm Problems
authors: C. E. Veni Madhavan
abstract: We present our perspectives on the current status of, integer factoring and discrete logarithm, algorithms underlying the strength of classical public-key cryptography protocols used in key-exchange, encryption and digital signatures. We present an expository overview of the algebraic, number-theoretic and algorithmic principles behind the canonical, powerful algorithms used in the factoring of large, composite RSA modulii. These cover the two main ideas of group order based methods, and quadratic congruence based methods. We provide the resource estimates for the record breaking factoring based on the general number field sieve. Next we present an overview of the algorithmic theory of quantum computation behind, the polynomial time Shor's quantum algorithm for, period finding in hidden subgroup structure problems. This algorithm has played a key role in advancing post-quantum cryptography, and also in the exciting, contemporary developments in quantum computing, networking, sensing, and materials science as a whole. Latest advances in quantum computing rest on a variety of physics, engineering, algorithms, compilation, hardware, software techniques. There are several tradeoffs based on number of qubits, coherence times, control issues, errors and fault tolerance. In this environment, nuances of mathematical ideas, behind every step of the intricate arithmetical and algebraic computations under quantum models plays a significant role. We provide an overview of some of the recent ideas behind such algorithms. We conclude with a recent deep question on the ultimate feasibility of ultra large-scale, error-free, discrete, quantum computations required typically in cryptanalysis.

title: Graph-Based Cryptographic Encoding and Epidemiological Modeling via Even Felicitous Labeling
authors: Narayanan NL, Gayathri S, Jamal Barakath, Avinash N, Nanthitha MM, Sampoornam M, Balaji V
abstract: In this work, we have identifified a way for encoding a secret message utilizing the GMJ (Graph Message Jumbled) Code and even felicitous labeling on fifive-star graphs K1,σ1 ∪ K1,σ2 ∪ K1,σ3 ∪ K1,σ4 ∪ K1,σ5 . For every star graph, we give two examples and use a Java program to apply alphabetical techniques to the Corona Number and Triangular Number. A strategy for labeling an even felicitous graph and flflowchart is provided for transforming plaintext into ciphertext (Picture Coding). Furthermore, we demonstrate an innovative application of these graph labeling techniques to epidemiological modeling through a detailed analysis of the SIR (Susceptible-Infected-Recovered) epidemic model on star networks. The paper shows how felicitous labeling can encode varying transmission probabilities and infection states, providing insights for targeted public health interventions. This interdisciplinary approach bridges cryptography, graph theory, and epidemiology, offffering both secure communication methods and practical disease spread modeling frameworks.

title: Optimizing Resource Allocation in Cloud Computing Environments using Reinforcement Learning
authors: MSR Prasad
journal: International Journal of Technology Management and Humanities
abstract: Cloud computing resource allocation remains a critical challenge, with organizations wasting an estimated $109 billion annually on idle or over-provisioned resources. Traditional allocation strategies—static provisioning, threshold-based autoscaling, and time-series forecasting—fail to capture the complex, non-stationary dynamics of modern cloud workloads characterized by bursty arrivals, heterogeneous resource demands, and multi-tenant interference effects.
